title: U.S. House · California's 37th District
area: Central Los Angeles, including Culver City, Inglewood, Baldwin Hills, Leimert Park, and View Park–Windsor Hills.

context.text: California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary. In the June 2, 2026 primary, incumbent Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D) placed first with 55.2% and Samantha Mota (D) placed second with 11.7%, so both Democrats advance to the November general election; no Republican advanced.

summary.text: Sydney Kamlager-Dove is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 37th District. She previously served in both houses of the California state Legislature and as president of the Los Angeles Community College District Board of Trustees.

background.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois, in 1972; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Southern California in 1994 and a master's degree in arts management and public policy from Carnegie Mellon University in 1996.
Worked as district director for then-State Senator Holly J. Mitchell and served as president of the Los Angeles Community College District Board of Trustees.
Served in the California State Assembly from 2018 to 2021 and the California State Senate from 2021 to 2022, before her election to Congress in 2022.

priorities.text: Says extending enhanced ACA tax credits and addressing the affordability crisis are urgent priorities, and has led oversight efforts on ICE conduct and foreign-policy matters as Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia.

positions.summary: Celebrated House passage of a three-year extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits, saying Democrats fought to prevent health care premiums from doubling for 22 million Americans.
positions.quote: Extending these tax credits is a simple, commonsense step to help families get by—one that 78 percent of Americans support.

positions.summary: Said Trump's tariffs created chaos for small businesses and drove up prices while doing little to protect American workers, and called for the administration to halt them and refund businesses.
positions.quote: These arbitrary tariffs have created chaos for small businesses and caused prices for nearly everything from groceries to clothes to skyrocket, all while doing next to nothing to protect American workers and industries.

positions.summary: Voted no on a DHS appropriations bill, citing ICE funding levels and conduct including the killing of a U.S. citizen and the detention of a constituent, and said she would give the agency no more funding.
positions.quote: No more blank checks for this rogue agency.

positions.summary: Says she will continue to support defensive military aid to Israel, such as Iron Dome, but will not support unconditional offensive military aid to the Netanyahu government, citing its use to prolong the Gaza war and expand West Bank annexation.
positions.quote: Even as I will continue to support the provision of defensive equipment to Israel like Iron Dome, I can no longer support unconditional offensive military aid to the Netanyahu government.

record.text: Was assigned to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs (Western Hemisphere Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Natural Resources in the 118th Congress (2023–2024).

candidates.name: Samantha Mota
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 11.7% of the vote

summary.text: Samantha Mota is a Democratic candidate running against incumbent Sydney Kamlager-Dove after placing second in the June 2026 top-two primary, describing her campaign as grassroots and community-focused.

background.text: Placed second in the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary with 11.7% of the vote (15,019 votes), advancing to a same-party general election against incumbent Sydney Kamlager-Dove.

priorities.text: Says her campaign is grassroots, community-focused, and transparent, and that she is running because the district needs new, bold, and transparent leadership.
priorities.quote: I'm running for Congress because we NEED representation. There has been a lack of new, bold, and transparent government and leadership in politics.

priorities.text: Says she is passionate about immigration reform, universal health care, family leave, and economic stability.
priorities.quote: The areas of public policy that I am passionate about are immigration reform, universal health care, Family Leave, and economic stability to heal the betrayal that have left our communities, neighborhoods, and nation abandoned and broken.

positions.summary: Lists universal health care as a policy area she is passionate about.
positions.quote: The areas of public policy that I am passionate about are immigration reform, universal health care, Family Leave, and economic stability to heal the betrayal that have left our communities, neighborhoods, and nation abandoned and broken.

researchNotes: Kamlager-Dove has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; her positions and priorities here are drawn from official House press releases on health care, tariffs, DHS/ICE funding, and military aid to Israel. Her generic issues subpages (health, economy, energy, education) had no substantive content beyond a placeholder message. Mota's positions come from her 2025-completed survey, which is brief.
